title: The War on Purity
author: Juan Domínguez del Corral
summary: Juan Domínguez del Corral of Ad Aeternum argues that contemporary culture is waging an open war on the virtue of purity, using a Sydney Sweeney gambling ad as a jumping-off point. He catalogs sexually charged advertising, prestige television, OnlyFans-driven fame, and industry-funded sex research as evidence that the world wants men to remain slaves to their impulses. Asking why, he draws on the Thomistic 'eight daughters of lust' to argue that sexual sin clouds the intellect and softens the will, and on St. Peter Damian to argue that lust is uniquely secret and self-enclosing. That concealment, he suggests, isolates men, corrodes male friendship and marriage, and may help explain the epidemic of male loneliness. The second half turns practical, pairing a sacramental life and prayer with a concrete protocol: removing triggers, abstaining from alcohol, changing one's identity, fasting, frequent confession, and staying busy. He closes by insisting that the battle cannot be won alone and requires surrender to God.
points: The author reads cultural sexualization in ads, entertainment, and sponsored research as a coordinated pressure against purity rather than coincidence.
Following Aquinas, he argues that persistent sexual sin weakens both intellect and will.
Drawing on Peter Damian, he argues lust is uniquely self-enclosing, and the resulting concealment undermines honesty in friendship and marriage.
His practical protocol includes removing triggers, avoiding alcohol, adopting the identity 'I am not a man who watches porn', fasting, and frequent confession.
He argues that attempts to quit pornography without spiritual work usually fail.
quotes: Most people who have given this some thought would agree that our culture has declared an open war against purity, and that it’s not a coincidence that millions of dollars are spent every single day trying to get you to fall into sexual immorality.

You can see now why the enemy would want you lustful: clouded by sexual sin, your intellectual power will be limited and your will will be softened, making it much more likely that you remain blind to the truth of God’s existence and incapable of pursuing the disciplines required to get there.
When a man is consumed by sexual immorality, he stops being capable of developing genuine relationships, because any authentic relationship requires the mutual knowledge of each other’s interior.
No relationship can flourish without honesty. A marriage even less so.

Lust is a physical and psychological problem, yes, but it’s also deeply spiritual. That’s why most attempts to quit porn and other forms of sexual immorality that do not include spiritual work eventually fail.
If there’s one thing I’d like you to take from this article, it’s this: the enemy wants you weak, dumb and addicted to your base impulses, and is using the machinery of culture to achieve that.
Only once you understand the overwhelming strength of the forces of impurity will you understand just how impossible it is to fight them alone.
